newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish debt/currency market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swedish debt/currency market closing report.

text.p: Swedish debt yields fell and the crown firmed on Monday as the decision to bring the italian lira back into the ERM-grid fuelled buying in most of Europe's high-yielders.
"It's not buying triggered by hopes of a Swedish ERM-link, we are just tailing other markets lower," said one dealer.

Six-month T-bills closed one basis point lower while 10-year bonds fell four basis points to yield 7.20 percent. At 1515 GMT, the mark had eased to 4.3750/80 crowns from 4.4045 crowns Friday afternoon.
Dealers were now focusing on the Riksbank's announcement of its new seven-day repo operation on Tuesday, the last in a series of four repos at a fixed rate of 4.60 percent.

A Reuter survey showed seven of 16 analysts expected the repo rate to be cut by five-25 basis points while the remaining nine expected an unchanged repo rate. These did not expect the central bank to trim the key interest rate again until it releases its next inflation report on December 17.
Sweden's October producer price figures were also due out on Tuesday and were expected to show a 0.1 percent drop in the month, for an annual fall of 4.4-5.0 percent in September.
